w: For the successful completion of the Bhadra murti installation festival, a total of 2,225 male and female volunteers were at work in 23 departments. But in 1969, when Yogiji Maharaj installed the mandir right here, there was no such corps of volunteers. If you count a corps, it was Swamishri's faith in Shriji Maharaj, and if you count strength, it was Swamishri's unbroken devotion to Shriji Maharaj and his devotion to his guru, Yogiji Maharaj. A priceless record of Swamishri's hard work at that time is found on page after page of the diaries he himself wrote. This is a golden documentary page of history.
A few of those original pages are presented here as a memento. Swamishri's notes in his own handwriting are presented as they are, and the same details have also been typed and placed below them.
On 23 April 1969, after the murti installation by Yogiji Maharaj, Swamishri immediately set to work on the seva of winding up.
In his diary of 24 April 1969 he notes: "Arrangements made to send back the pandals, tents, utensils and so on; dispatched in the trucks of Bhailubha Bapu, Jambha and the sack merchant Sheth."
In the days after that, Swamishri remained busy with the wind up. Finally, in his diary of 26 April 1969 he notes: "Today everything was sent back. Not a single thing went missing."

Amid so much busyness, that not a single item went missing, from utensils, mattresses and quilts brought from outside to things large and small, shows how deeply and minutely Swamishri must have planned!! This festival shows Swamishri's skilful leadership.
Bhimjibhai, who was constantly with him as a volunteer helping in the seva, says about the wind up:

"After the installation was over, when Yogiji Maharaj left for Gondal in the evening, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was getting the wind up work done at the dharmashala. When Yogiji Maharaj's car, a DeSoto, set off, Pramukh Swami said to me, 'Bapa is going to Gondal, so come, let us go and meet him.' We went to Bapa. Bapa rolled down the car window, gave his blessings, and told Pramukh Swami to finish the wind up work and come to Gondal after five days. We finished all the wind up work in five days and went to Gondal with Pramukh Swami."

ds.t: The wind up at Bhadra in 1969
w: To complete the Bhadra murti installation festival successfully, a total of 2,225 male and female volunteers were at work in 23 departments, but in 1969, when Yogiji Maharaj installed the murtis in the mandir right here, there was no such corps of volunteers. Whether you count it as the corps or as the strength, it was Pramukh Swami Maharaj's faith in Shriji Maharaj, his unbroken devotion to Shriji Maharaj and his devotion to his guru, Yogiji Maharaj. A priceless record of Swamishri's hard work at that time is found on page after page of the diaries he himself wrote. This is a golden documentary page of history.

Some of those original pages are presented here as a remembrance. The notes Swamishri made in his own handwriting are presented as they are, and the same details have also been typed and placed below them.
After the murti installation by Yogiji Maharaj on that day, Swamishri immediately got busy with the seva of winding up
In his diary for 24 April 1969 he notes, "Arrangements made to send back the pavilions, tents, utensils and so on; dispatched in the trucks of Bhailubha Bapu, Jambha and the sack merchant Sheth."
In the days that followed, Swamishri remained busy with the wind up. Finally, in his diary for 26 April 1969, he notes, "Today everything was sent back. Not a single item was missing."

Amid so much busyness, that not a single item was missing, from the utensils, mattresses and quilts brought from outside to things big and small, shows how deeply and minutely Swamishri must have planned!! This festival gives an introduction to Swamishri's skilful leadership.
Bhimjibhai, who constantly remained with him as a helper volunteer in the seva, says about the wind up,

"After the installation was over, when Yogiji Maharaj left for Gondal in the evening, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was getting the wind up work done at the dharamshala. When Yogiji Maharaj's car, a DeSoto, was leaving, Pramukh Swami said to me, 'Bapa is going to Gondal, come, let us go and meet him.' We went to Bapa. Bapa lowered the car window and gave his blessings, and told Pramukh Swami to finish the wind up work and come to Gondal after five days. We finished all the wind up work in five days and went to Gondal with Pramukh Swami."

The evening assembly was held at the Krishna Mandir hall. The president of the Hindu Mahajan and renowned Shri Kanakshi Khimji offered a shawl and honored Swamishri. The assembly agenda of discourses, bhajans and Swamishri's blessings delighted the audience.
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for three Swaminarayan hari mandirs in Bhavnagar district, namely, Kundhada, Jaspara (Mandva) and Pipaliya.
Swamishri performed the foundation-stone laying ceremony of a students' hostel in the mandir precincts.

The evening satsang assembly was dedicated to 'Teacher's Day'. Kishores and yuvaks performed a drama 'A Tree is Known From its Fruits' which depicted true incidents regarding how educated and virtuous satsangi youths have inspired character-building in society through anti-addiction drives, etc. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly.
At 10.30 a.m. Swamishri departed for London from Sardar Patel International Airport, Amdavad. Covering a distance of 6,874 km Swamishri landed at Heathrow Airport at 7.05 p.m. (IST) (2.35 p.m. GMT).
Swamishri was given a warm welcome at the Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
ph: Swamishri accepts the devotion of UK Satsang Mandal through a unique garland prepared by Mahila Mandal

w: In the evening assembly BAPS youths performed a drama, ‘Bharat nu Sohamanu Swapna’, which portrayed icons of self-confidence, self-realisation, austerity and others from India’s glorious past. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Today people do not like religious talks. The atmosphere is such that one forgets about the importance of character and culture. Because of TV and websites the lessons of self-discipline are fading. When there is no discrimination between right and wrong one becomes inclined towards bad things. When one listens to bad things and eats non-veg then how can one do satsang? Yogiji Maharaj willed for a better, character-based society. Through his desire the activities are going on. His work was to redeem all and make them happier. He was pure and in control of his ten senses and speech…”

Over 8,000 devotees were present in Swamishri’s morning puja. The diksha mahapuja was performed during Swamishri’s puja. Thereafter, Swamishri initiated 21 parshads into the sadhu-fold and 30 sadhaks into the parshad-fold. As each youth approached Swamishri to receive diksha and the guru mantra, Swamishri blessed them with some words of special guidance. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Parents happily give their only sons whom they have raised and educated… They gladly present them at the feet of God… for this they will gain many merits and blessings. “Sadhus serve to raise the awareness of dharma in the country, free thousands from addictions, help thousands shed bad habits, and encourage people to observe niyams and walk the spiritual path. The sadhus will serve society, the country and God and gain liberation for their atma. “To observe the niyams of a sadhu, please God and guide thousands onto the path of God requires courage. Such courage has been shown by the parents and by the sons. “The youths who become sadhus will truly become ekantik and will gain the strength to observe niyams and dharma, agna and upasana and please Maharaj.”

ds.t: Return it better than we found it
w: After finishing breakfast, Mahant Swami Maharaj chose to have his bath, because today he had to leave early to go to Kolkata.

By the time Swamishri came out after his bath, most of the room had been packed up. Swamishri's eyes fell on his bed. The sheet was a little creased and the pillows were not in their places. Swamishri himself began smoothing out the creases on the sheet and arranging the pillows neatly.
In the hurry to leave, the attendant said, "Swami! This is not yours."

What the attendant meant was: "The sheets and pillows used for you have all been packed, and now only the sheets and pillows of this place are left, which the volunteers will set right after we leave!"
And besides, there was a hurry to leave just then.
But Swamishri said, "No, we must set it right and give it back better than we found it."
In what words can we describe this virtue? In which scripture shall we go looking for this virtue? Truly, the great sadhu, who possesses so many such virtues, is an ideal for us in every field.

Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived in Kolkata by plane at 12.14. Coming out of the plane, Swamishri sat in a helicopter. At the very start there was a wait of 15 to 20 minutes for refuelling. After that, another fifteen minutes or so passed... but the helicopter still did not take off. It turned out that the helicopter was not getting permission to fly.
Hariprakashdas Swami asked Swamishri, "When this happens, don't you get fed up?"
"There is joy; the remembrance of Bhagwan keeps going," said Swamishri, making the gesture of turning a mala.
Following on from the talk of enduring, Swamishri said, "Even the great sadhu has to endure."
Singing Swamishri's glory, Digantbhai said, "But you are sitting so calmly and are so steady that it does not seem you have to endure anything." (That is, you do not let it show.)
"Why should I show it? To whom should I show it? What would I gain by showing it?" Swamishri said with feeling.
And truly, Swamishri did not show how much he was enduring; but the attendants saw that Swamishri was drenched in sweat. And Swamishri's skin was turning red because of the sun.
Digantbhai asked, "Swami! Will there be such tight security for going to Akshardham too?"
"No, straight to Akshardham," said Swamishri, snapping his fingers.
Hariprakashdas Swami asked, "Now that we are talking about Akshardham, how does one get to Akshardham?"
"This is Akshardham itself," said Swamishri.
Digantbhai said, "Even so, we do not feel the happiness."
Swamishri said, "The reason is our nature."
Hariprakashdas Swami said, "If you show grace, our natures will go away."
"We have attained the refuge of Bhagwan; keep it firm," Swamishri answered.
Digantbhai said, "Then Akshardham is certain, isn't it?"
"Certain," said Swamishri, snapping his fingers.
Hariprakashdas Swami said, "That is only because we have met you; otherwise attaining Akshardham would wear us out."

Swamishri immediately turned the talk into a flow of devotion to his gurus, saying, "We have received a powerful guru parampara, haven't we! We have got the key. Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj, Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, whoever one met in his time, each one is a key."
Hariprakashdas Swami said, "We have got the key, but we do not recognise it."
"That is exactly what has to be done," said Swamishri.
Digantbhai asked, "What should we do to know how to use that key?"
"Do this." Saying this, Swamishri pointed to the helicopter and the situation around it.
Hariprakashdas Swami tried to decipher Swamishri's hint and said, "To keep patience in such a situation."
Endorsing this, Swamishri said, "That is it, keep patience and stay joyful."
"But how can one keep patience in this?"
"Understand it as Bhagwan's wish."
"But can Bhagwan wish such a thing?"
"Whatever he does, he does for the good."
"Please make it so that we too have such patience."
Swamishri said, "If these three things come, humility, patience and forgiveness, one goes beyond the body. Identification with the body goes away."
Hariprakashdas Swami said, "Then one would attain Akshardham!"
Swamishri said, "Once identification with the body has gone, the happiness of Akshardham comes right here."
Hariprakashdas Swami said, "Please show grace so that our identification with the body goes away and the understanding you have spoken of becomes firm in our souls."
In reply, Swamishri only smiled meaningfully.
Permission to fly the helicopter had still not come. It was a situation in which one could easily get exasperated, but Swamishri was steady.

In this situation, singing Swamishri's glory, Hariprakashdas Swami said, "You are so powerful that countless millions of universes float in each of your pores, and yet you show such powerlessness; that too is surely your great power, isn't it!"
"All that is as you understand it," said Swamishri, leaving the matter to the one who understands.

Hariprakashdas Swami said, "This is what Shriji Maharaj has said in the Vachanamrut: to be forbearing despite being powerful is something no one can do. This virtue is seen in you, and also the virtues of humility, patience and forgiveness that you spoke of earlier."
Again giving all the credit to Bhagwan, Swamishri said, "It happens by Bhagwan's wish."
By now even the pilots had begun to get thoroughly exasperated. Swamishri said, "What can they do, poor things? The situation itself has arisen like this!"
Hariprakashdas Swami said, "Cast your glance on us so that even in such a situation we may have patience and joy."

Swamishri said, "That is exactly what has to be done. We have received such an attainment, so stay joyful! We have met Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, so keep the joy of that. Understand everyone as divine, see them as forms of Brahman."
"Swami! That is exactly what is hard."
"But that is exactly what has to be done." Then he added, "And it is not that we just have to see them as divine; they truly are divine. Now we have to believe it; if we do not, it is our loss."
Taking up the point about divinity, Digantbhai asked, "Swami! Are all those you have met divine too?"
Swamishri said "Yes."
"You have come to this earth, so is the earth divine too?"
"Yes."
"You have come into this universe, so is this universe divine too?"
Swamishri nodded yes.

It was 2.45. There was still no news of permission. Finally a decision was taken: "Take Swamishri to the mandir by car." But then another problem cropped up. Now Swamishri and the sadhus were forbidden to leave the airport. Swamishri was watching and listening to all this attentively, but there was not a single trace of exasperation or anger on his face.
Seeing Swamishri's steadiness, the verse of the Gita comes to mind:
"Esha brahmi sthitih Partha nainam prapya vimuhyati,
Sthitvasyam antakale'pi brahmanirvanam ricchati." (This is the brahmic state, O Partha; attaining it, one is not deluded; remaining in it even at the hour of death, one attains the bliss of Brahman.)
Hariprakashdas Swami said, "What is this? No permission is coming at all."
Then, turning this back into the flow of the earlier discussion, the sadhus said, "In the same way, permission will be needed to go to Akshardham, won't it? Please give us permission."
"Since we have met Bhagwan and the sadhu, permission has already been given. We have already attained Akshardham," said Swamishri.
Digantbhai asked, "Since you have met us, the work is done, isn't it!"
Swamishri said "Yes."
Meanwhile, through the sadhus' efforts, permission to go out was granted.
Swamishri called Atmaswarupdas Swami and said, "Whatever we had agreed, all the payment must be made."
Oh... what a compassionate nature!
Turmeric does not give up its yellowness, nor the mango its six flavours;
The virtuous do not give up their virtues, nor the slave his faults.

The discussion, which covered many subjects such as remembering Bhagwan, enduring, keeping patience, understanding who the doer is, enjoying the attainment and understanding others as divine, came to an end, and finally Swamishri's car left the airport. The hands of the clock showed 3.00.
Remember, this inspiring discussion took place without any planning, while waiting at the airport for almost two and three quarter hours!

Arriving at the Kolkata mandir, Mahant Swami Maharaj had darshan of Thakorji upstairs in the mandir and came to the Abhishek Mandapam. He performed abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni and did circumambulation. But during the darshan and dandvats so far, the attendants had noticed that Swamishri was tired from the wait he had to endure in the sun and from today's heavy and long journey. Tiredness was clearly visible on his face. So they requested Swamishri, "Please leave the dandvats here." But Swamishri said in a pleading tone, "Five." That is, "Let me do five dandvats. It will be fine." Saying this, Swamishri began doing dandvats.
Adverse circumstances could not weaken Swamishri's devotion.

Today Mahant Swami Maharaj himself was tired from such a long and unexpected journey on the ekadashi day and from the unbearable heat he had to endure while waiting. According to Swamishri's wish, the evening meal was postponed. The sadhus began saying to Swamishri, "Today you had a lot of trouble."
Swamishri said, "Bhagwan's wish."

One sadhu said, "Today you endured so much hardship, and still you met every devotee calmly, without the slightest hurry. And you had darshan of Thakorji just as calmly. Even though the attendants and sadhus said no, you did dandvat, so you did not let any lapse come into your devotion either. Today you forgot the body and behaved as the atma."
The sadhus said, "Today we all saw that your hands were trembling as you did dandvat, and twice you even lost your balance a little."
Swamishri said "Yes," accepting it.
The sadhus said, "Seeing this, we felt it would be better if you did not do dandvat now, but still you did them."
Referring to the illnesses Swamishri takes upon himself, the sadhus said, "And you should use your divine power to remove your illness too."
Swamishri laughed and said, "It is not to be used for oneself."
Shantpurushdas Swami said, "Then give me whatever illness you have."
Swamishri refused, saying, "It is divine."
The clear message was that even the great sadhu's illness is divine. Even through illness, he brings many into contact with himself and liberates those souls.

Swamishri no longer had any desire to eat, so it was decided to put him to bed. Swamishri too agreed. Swamishri was put to bed. Swamishri said, "Today at the airport there was a good discussion with Hariprakash Swami."

Oh! The amazing thing was that Swamishri had had to endure so much hardship at the airport, but he had not uttered a single word about it or made a single complaint about it; only what had been good in it
did Swamishri remember!!

st.t: Assam Governor and Acting Meghalaya Governor Banwarilal Purohit Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: On Sunday 23 April 2017, the Governor of Assam and the Acting Governor of Meghalaya Shri Banwarilal Purohit visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, a grand mandir showcasing and celebrating Indian art, culture, traditions, and values, through its breathtaking stone carvings and exhibitions.

On behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj – Spiritual Head of Swaminarayan Akshardham and BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha – senior sadhus traditionally welcomed the Governor with a garland of flowers, tilaka (vermillion powder) and the tying of the sacred kalva (sacred thread) at the Mayur Dwar (Peacock Gate).

Governor Purohit first visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir, where he witnessed the world’s ‘Largest Comprehensive Hindu Temple’. After paying respects to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, he admired the Mandir’s art and architecture. He learned how His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the former spiritual leader of BAPS, inspired thousands of volunteers and artisans to create the mandir to share the message of love, peace, tolerance, non-violence, co-existence and global harmony.

Governor Purohit marveled at the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth) that includes 148 life-sized carved stone elephants depicting message of social harmony, peace and spirituality. He offered prayers for world peace and harmony by offering ‘abhishek’, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy rivers, lakes and ponds across India, on the sacred image of Shri Neelkanth Varni (the teenage form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan).

Thereafter, Governor Purohit experienced the educational exhibitions: Sahajanand Darshan (Hall of Values) – robotic shows depicting the ideals of nonviolence, honest, harmony and faith, Neelkanth Darshan – a Giant Screen film on the epic journey of Neelkanth Varni throughout India and Sanskruti Vihar – a cultural voyage that sails through 10,000 years of India’s glorious heritage, highlighting India’s contributions to humanity through the ages. Finally, they witnessed the Sahaj Anand Water Show , a theatrical presentation about an ancient Upanishad story with modern fountains, projections, lasers and fire.

Attending the satsang assembly at the Pramukh Swami Auditorium, Governor Purohit was honoured by Sadhu Narendraprasad (Acharya Swamiji) with a garland of flowers and prasad. Addressing the assembly, the Governor said, “Pramukh Swami Maharaj is truly a form of God himself. He is always into selfless service and preaching spirituality. Many invaders have tried to diminish Indian culture. However, Indian culture is still alive in its whole form because of its spiritual base and the efforts of greats like Bhagwan Swaminarayan, his sadhus and his devotees who have been performing the sacred work of preserving spiritual values on this Earth.”

Completing the visit, the Governor of Assam and the Acting Governor of Meghalaya Shri Banwarilal Purohit wrote in the visitor’s book, “ Today’s visit to the Swaminarayan (Akshardham) Temple will be remembered by me as a memorable day of my life. In one word, if I had to describe the Swaminarayan temple, it is totality unimaginable. We were thrilled to see Bhartiya Sanskruti (Indian culture) in totality. This institution is providing Dharma and Sanskruti in our country. There cannot be any comparison with any institution – not only in India but in the world. Total dedication and selfless sacrifice of swamijis and volunteer is the foundation of this institution. My many many thanks to Mahant Swamiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj for giving me this wonderful opportunity on this auspicious day of Ekadashi. My regards to all the swamijis of the institution.
